title: Tenant Fairness Auditing & Reconciliation Framework
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This page defines an operational framework and automation blueprint for detecting, auditing, and reconciling tenant-level fairness issues across Redwood's multi-tenant inference platform. Fairness is defined as adherence to configured resource allocations, queueing priorities, and cost/latency entitlements for paying tenants. The goal is to provide reproducible audits, operator runbooks, dashboards, and safe automated remediation primitives.

Goals
-----
- Detect deviations from expected allocation/priority behavior within 15 minutes of occurrence.
- Produce a reproducible audit record for every detected deviation that includes raw telemetry, operator actions, and reconciliation results.
- Provide dashboards and alerts that are actionable for on-call and capacity owners.
- Define safe automated reconciliation actions (reclaims, re-weighting, throttles) with human approval gates and rollback windows.
- Close the loop with retrospective analysis and continuous improvements to allocation policies.

Scope
-----
Applies to: Hosted API and Dedicated pools running Redwood serving runtime where multiple tenants share a scheduler, queueing layer, or GPU pool. Excludes fully isolated Private (VPC) deployments where tenant isolation is customer-managed.

Definitions
-----------
- Tenant fairness event: any measurable breach where a tenant's observed resource share or latency deviates from the entitlement band for >= 5 minutes.
- Entitlement: configured share, e.g., reserved throughput, burst credits, or priority queue assignment.
- Reconciliation action: operator or automated change applied to restore entitlement alignment (e.g., reclaim burst credits, adjust weight, throttle noisy tenant).

Signals, SLIs and thresholds
---------------------------
Primary SLIs (per-tenant):
- p50, p95, p99 latency (generation path) — threshold: p95 within configured entitlement multiplier (default 1.5x baseline for plan).
- Effective token cost per inference (tokens-in * compute-cost-profile) — threshold: 2x expected for sustained 30m.
- Queue time (scheduler wait) — threshold: > 200ms for > 5% of requests in 10m window.
- Token throughput relative to reserved capacity — threshold: sustained 120% of reservation for 15m.
- Error rate (5xx + model-swap rejections) — threshold: > 0.5% over 10m.

Secondary signals (correlation):
- Kernel preemption events, GPU-metrics (SM utilization, GPU memory pressure), network retransmits, KV cache miss rate.

Dashboard & Alerting spec
------------------------
High-level dashboard panels (Grafana):
1) Tenant Fairness Overview: per-tenant sparkline of p95 latency, queue time, and share delta against entitlement.
2) Heatmap: percent of tenants with >20% share deviation in last 6h.
3) Recent fairness incidents: list panel with incident id, start, duration, primary cause, resolution, and owner.
4) Audit pipeline backlog: number of pending audits, last processed timestamp, processing latency.
5) Reconciliation action outcomes: success rate, rollback rate, and operator confirmation latency.

Suggested alert rules (PromQL-style)
- Alert: tenant_high_share_deviation
  Expr: max_over_time((tenant_share_current - tenant_share_expected)/tenant_share_expected[15m]) > 0.2
  For: 10m
  Severity: P2
  Runbook: follow "On-detect: Investigate tenant share deviation" (section below)

- Alert: tenant_p95_latency_entitlement_breach
  Expr: increase(tenant_request_count{tenant=~"$tenant"}[10m]) > 0 and 
        histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(tenant_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="$tenant"}[5m])) by (le)) > (tenant_p95_entitlement_seconds * 1.5)
  For: 5m
  Severity: P1 for high-revenue tenants, P2 otherwise

Audit pipeline architecture (high level)
-------------------------------------
- Ingest: stream tenant-tagged runtime telemetry (latency buckets, tokens, queue events) into the platform observability pipeline (Kafka -> parquet lake).
- Enrichment: join telemetry with tenant entitlement metadata (plan, reserved throughput, burst credits, priority tier) in the audit worker.
- Detection: run windowed fairness detectors (sliding 5m windows) producing candidate events with evidence pointers (trace ids, raw spans).
- Persist: store canonical audit records in the Fairness Audit Store (S3 parquet + index in Postgres for quick lookups).
- Reconciliation engine: decides action based on policy and escalation level; actions are recorded in the audit record.
- Reporting: generate a daily fairness digest and a 30-day SLA variance report.

Data model (CSV schema example for audit export)
- Columns: incident_id, start_ts, end_ts, tenant_id, tenant_plan, detected_metric, observed_value, expected_value, evidence_path, owner, action_taken, action_status, notes

Operator runbook: On-detect — Investigate tenant share deviation
------------------------------------------------------------
1) Triage: open the audit record (audit_id in alert). Confirm signals: p95 latency, queue time, effective token cost.
2) Quick queries (run in Observability UI or click-to-run templates):
   - tenant_requests_total{tenant="$tenant", region="$region"} by (model) [10m]
   - tenant_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{tenant="$tenant"} by (le) [10m]
   - tenant_tokens_consumed_total{tenant="$tenant"} [30m]
3) Correlate infrastructure signals: GPU preemptions, kernel-switch counts, pod restarts during window.
4) Identify likely root cause buckets (choose one): noisy-tenant burst, model variant change, scheduler mis-weight, infra degradation.
5) If cause is noisy tenant and entitlement exceeded:
   - If tenant is on burst credits: check burst balance API (curl -X GET https://internal-api/tenants/$tenant/burst)
   - If burst credits exhausted: consider reclaiming soft-burst credits per policy (requires operator approval for premium tenants).
6) If scheduler mis-weight suspected: check current weight table (/etc/platform/weights or weights service API) and roll back last weight change if within 30 minutes.
7) Document findings in audit record, set provisional owner (oncall, capacity-owner, account-ops), and escalate if revenue-impacting.

Automated reconciliation patterns and safety gates
------------------------------------------------
Allowed autopilot actions (configurable per tier):
- Soft throttle: apply a token-per-second cap at the scheduler for the offending tenant for up to 10 minutes.
- Weight adjustment: temporary -10% weight for low-priority tenants when global contention detected.
- Burst reclaim: transfer unused burst credits from pool to affected tenants (requires 2FA operator approval for >1m tokens).

Safety controls:
- Every automated action creates an audit record and a 5-minute human confirmation window for high-revenue tenants.
- Rollback window: automated actions are automatically reverted after 15 minutes unless approved extension is recorded.
- Canary gating: autopilot actions must be validated in synthetic workload lab before being unlocked for production.

Reconciliation action example (noisy tenant reclaim)
1) Create incident with severity and owner.
2) Execute: platform-cli tenant throttle --tenant $tenant --rate 50r/s --reason "autobot reclaim noisy tenant"
3) Verify: p95 latency for affected victim tenants drops below entitlement threshold in 5-10m.
4) Close incident with remediation notes and schedule a billing credit check if appropriate.

Escalation matrix
-----------------
- Oncall Platform (P1/P2 triage) — first responder, provides temporary mitigations.
- Capacity Owner (team: eng-platform) — config changes, weight table rollbacks, capacity provisioning.
- Customer Success (CS) — if tenant is enterprise, CS MUST be notified within 30 minutes of P1 incidents.
- Legal/Security — if incident may involve data residency or exfiltration anomalies.

Retrospective and continuous improvement loop
-------------------------------------------
- Post-incident, attach the audit record to a 2-week retrospective if any of: SLA breach >10 minutes, billing impact >$500, or automated action rollback rate >5%.
- Readouts: 1) root cause taxonomy frequency, 2) time-to-detection, 3) operator action success rate, 4) automation rollback fraction.
- Action owner: platform-ops team to track 90-day remediation backlog.

Rollout plan and milestones
--------------------------
- Phase 0 (30 days) — instrumentation: tag all runtime telemetry with tenant_id and persist to Kafka; create basic tenant overview Grafana dashboard.
- Phase 1 (60 days) — detection: deploy sliding-window detectors and the Fairness Audit Store; enable manual runbook flows.
- Phase 2 (90 days) — controlled autopilot: unlock soft throttle and weight adjustments behind feature flag; runbook enforced for premium tenants.
- Phase 3 (120+ days) — evaluation: run A/B on autopilot policies, refine thresholds, and publish the first 30-day fairness report.

Ownership & contacts
--------------------
- Product owner: Marco Ruiz (platform product)
- Engineering lead: Aisha Patel (eng-platform) — primary owner for rollout and automation safety
- Oncall rota: eng-platform oncall (see team wiki for pager schedule)

Appendix: Example queries and artifacts
-------------------------------------
Example PromQL to compute per-tenant share delta: 
  tenant_share_current = sum(rate(tenant_tokens_consumed_total[5m])) by (tenant) / sum(rate(tenant_tokens_consumed_total[5m]))
  tenant_share_expected loaded from entitlement store, join in downstream transformer.

Example CSV export row:
  2026-02-08T12:03:14Z,2026-02-08T12:18:22Z,inc-20260208-0007,tenant_42,pro-plan,p95_latency,1.48s,0.75s,s3://fairness-audit/2026/02/08/inc-0007.parquet,team-ops,soft-throttle,applied

Related work and next steps
---------------------------
- Integrate this framework with billing reconciliation so that tenant-visible credits/adjustments are reflected automatically.
- Add model-aware fairness detectors that account for model architecture cost variance (quantization, seq len).
- Expand reporting to surface fairness KPIs to Sales & CS weekly dashboards for transparency.

--------------------
